newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia PGM export system to stay - FinMin official.
newsitem.headline: Russia PGM export system to stay - FinMin official.

text.p: Russia does not intend to change the way its state precious metals export agency Almazjuvelirexport handles sales abroad of platinum group metals (PGM), a Finance Ministry official said on Tuesday.

"Almazjuvelirexport will remain as before," said Vladimir Rybkin, head of the ministry's precious metals section, when asked if Russian producers might be allowed to handle their own exports and bypass the agency.
"It will, for some time, remain as it has been."
But Rybkin said the ministry was preparing documents that could liberalise the way in which domestic platinum, gold and silver output is financed.
"We consider these metals more or less liquid and changes could help producers," he said, adding that there would be no changes to palladium.
Rybkin said the ministry was preparing recommendations for changes to the state prices offered to domestic precious metal producers.
"The changes will give more freedom to commercial banks as well as to producers," he said. He declined to be more specific.

When asked about Russian Norilsky Nickel's 0#NKEL.RUO NKEL.RTS desire to sell its own precious metals output, he said, "In my view, such an activity should remain a state undertaking. But in principle they are free to go to the government (with the proposal) if they wish."
The ministry plays a key role in Russia's precious metals export policies.
Rybkin declined to say when the ministry's recommendations might be discussed at government level.
A Norilsk spokesman said on Monday that the group planned to hold talks with the government on doing its own exports.
